stages.name: Measuring unemployment
stages.title: Measuring unemployment
stages.sub: How economists define and count unemployment, and why the two main measures give different numbers.

steps.q: A retiree and a student are not working or looking. A jobless 30-year-old is looking. Who counts in the labour force?
steps.wrong: All three, since none of them have a job
steps.hint: The labour force is about people who are in or seeking work, not everyone without a job.

steps.q: Among economically active people, some have a job and some don't, though they want one and can start. Which group are we measuring?
steps.right: Those without a job who want and can take one
steps.wrong: Everyone who is not currently working
steps.hint: Think about who is left out once you remove people who already have a job.

steps.q: To count the unemployed, the government adds up everyone claiming out-of-work benefits each month. What kind of count is this?
steps.right: A count based on benefit records
steps.wrong: A count based on a survey of households
steps.hint: This method uses administrative records, not a survey asking people questions.

steps.q: A jobless person is actively hunting for work but gets no benefits, so isn't in the benefit records. Would the survey still count them?
steps.right: Yes, if they answer that they are looking for work
steps.wrong: No, only benefit records can count them
steps.hint: The survey asks about job-seeking behaviour, not about benefit eligibility.
